label: D1: high after reaching S1, low after S2; GO: high when belief favours S2 / after a2 / unrewarded
terms: (phase == D1) * table(prev_state, {1: 1, 2: -1}) ;; (phase == D1) * table(prev_action, {1: -1, 2: 1}) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * np.tanh(belief_lo / 2) ;; (phase == GO) * table(prev_action, {1: -1, 2: 1}) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * table(prev_state, {1: -1, 2: 1}) ;; (phase == D2) * np.tanh(belief_lo / 2)
explanation: Raw reset gate r of unit 17 (always on; timing alone R^2 0.64, D2 near-saturated ~0.97). Beyond timing, D1 is dominated by the previous trial reached state: about +0.25 if it was S1 and -0.25 if S2 (a 0.5 swing), with a small extra +0.04 after choosing a2; the previous reward adds almost nothing at D1. At GO it tracks the inferred good state: lower when the ideal-observer belief favours S1 (tanh(belief_lo/2) weight -0.09), higher after an a2 choice (+0.07 per side), and lower after a rewarded trial (-0.11, slightly less so if that reward came from S2). D2 shows a small belief effect of the same sign. All terms are observed-only (no model value/policy, no future vars). Test R^2 beyond timing 0.716 (dev 0.723), vs observed-only ceiling 0.81 and all-cue ceiling 0.85; the earlier policy-based explanation (policy decile alone 0.44) is matched here by belief plus last-trial cues, so little is lost. Residual misses: GO after unrewarded trials is under-predicted and D1 after a1 S1 u over-predicted (sigmoid saturation / pattern interactions).

issues: The 8 terms (test R^2 beyond timing 0.716) score below the plain phase x last-trial lookup table in the profile (0.75). They are underfitting, not close to the ceiling.

The GO reward effect is mis-specified. The terms only have (phase==GO)*(prev_reward==1), and the intercept is shared across phases, so GO cannot get its own offset after unrewarded trials. Misses on the original terms show GO mean error +0.045 and systematic under-prediction at GO after unrewarded trials: a2 S2 u +0.156, a1 S2 u +0.149, a1 S1 u +0.112, a2 S1 u +0.081. Replacing that term with (phase==GO)*table(prev_reward,{0:1,1:-1}) gives weight +0.127 per side, about a 0.25 swing, not the -0.11 claimed. Test R^2 rises to 0.784 and those misses shrink to at most +0.063.
The explanation says these GO-unrewarded misses are 'likely interactions or saturation'. They are not. They disappear with one main-effect reward contrast at GO.

The claim that the previous reward 'adds almost nothing at D1' is too strong. The profile residuals at D1 are a1 S1 r +0.246 vs a1 S1 u +0.156, and a2 S1 r +0.319 vs a2 S1 u +0.263. A D1 reward contrast table(prev_reward,{0:-1,1:1}) fits +0.028 per side and raises test R^2 to 0.790. The original D1 rewarded indicator got weight +0.002 only because of the same shared-intercept problem.

The core claims do hold: at D1 the gate tracks the previous state (+/-0.25), at GO it is lower when belief favours S1 (about -0.10 on tanh(belief_lo/2)), a2 raises it at GO (+0.06), and the D2 belief effect is small (-0.03). No future variables are used.
